title: Boundary tag from the marker tape
statement: For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and every input-head position $p\in\{0,\ldots,n+1\}$, let $b$ be false if the one-cell marker tape has its $1$ at coordinate $p$, and true otherwise. If $p=0$, then $b$ is false; if $p=n+1$, then $b$ is true. No condition on $b$ is imposed at interior positions.
hypotheses_covered: A head position $p$ among the $n+2$ positions
The tag $b$ determined by whether the marker tape has a $1$ at $p$
replaced:
For every head position $p \in \{0, 1, \dots, n+1\}$ on an input of length
$n$ (with its two boundary blanks), the Boolean flag ``the marker tape
carrying a single mark at coordinate $0$ does not show its mark at coordinate
$p$'' satisfies the boundary-tag contract of the clamped virtual-move
operation: the flag is false at the left boundary $p = 0$ and true at the
right blank $p = n+1$, including when the input is empty.
